log.why: Test the leading candidate rpoB directly; a positive result yields ~88% confidence for a quick publication, while a negative rules it out.
Treating at 10 uM splits Ticket 2's prior probability mass closest to 50/50 (0.38 vs 0.62) for maximum information.
Testing leading candidate hisG (0.419) splits posterior cleanly and confirms it to ~0.89 if phenotype is lost.
Testing 3 µM cleanly separates the top candidate 10 µM from lower thresholds after the positive 10 µM response.
Testing {sodA, recA} splits Ticket 3's prior mass nearly 50/50 and lets the plate incubate while we publish Ticket 1.
Ticket 1 has a strong 0.890 posterior for hisG after two plates; publishing now secures time and plate bonuses while freeing a ticket slot.
Testing sodA cleanly resolves sodA versus recA while overlapping incubation with upcoming bench actions.
Knock out {sodA, gyrA} splits the prior nearly 50/50 (0.491) and lets the plate incubate while publishing Ticket 2 next.
Testing gyrA cleanly resolves the sodA vs gyrA tie while incubating during upcoming paper submissions for Tickets 2 and 3.
Ticket 2 has only 9 seconds left and a strong 0.702 posterior for 10 µM based on response at 10 µM but not 3 µM.
Ticket 3 expires in 8s and sodA has a strong 0.882 posterior after two knockouts.
E3 splits Ticket 6's posterior evenly at 3 µM (0.508 vs 0.492) and can incubate while we publish Ticket 4.
E3 splits Ticket 5's prior nearly evenly (0.48 vs 0.52) and can incubate while we publish Ticket 4.
Ticket 4 has only 5 seconds left and sodA has a strong 0.793 posterior from E8 and E5.
Testing gyrA maximizes single-plate expected accuracy on Ticket 7 by confirming gyrA on phenotype loss or boosting ftsZ otherwise.
E2 splits the dominant 1 µM and 3 µM hypotheses nearly evenly while leaving time to publish twice.
